hints: The empty subset is always included.
With n elements, the power set contains exactly 2^n subsets.
Represent each subset choice with n binary bits.
If bit i is 1, include nums[i]; otherwise exclude it.
title: Subsets Problem

notes: The order of the returned subsets does not matter. Each subset preserves the relative order of elements from nums.
constraints: All the numbers of nums are unique.
content.inputFormat: Single line: JSON array of all arguments, e.g. [arg1, arg2, ...]

sampleTestCases.explanation: There are 2^3 = 8 subsets, including the empty subset and the complete array. The subsets are shown in a deterministic order for the example.
For one element, the power set contains the empty subset and the subset containing that element.

content.problemStatement:
You receive an integer array `nums` of **unique** elements, output *all possible* *subsets* *(the power set)*.

The solution set **must not** contain duplicate subsets. The task is to output the solution in **any order**.

notes: The problem permits any subset order; the platform comparator must therefore compare the returned collection order-independently.
The boilerplates emit subsets in deterministic bitmask order.
There are exactly 2^n distinct subsets for n unique input elements.
The output itself contains Θ(n * 2^n) element occurrences in the worst case, so output-sized space is unavoidable.
solution.approach: Enumerate every bitmask from 0 through 2^n - 1. Bit i indicates whether nums[i] belongs to the subset represented by that mask.

better.complexity: O(n * 2^n) time and O(n * 2^n) space including the returned output.
better.description: Build the answer iteratively. Start with [[]]. For each number, copy every existing subset and append the number to each copy, doubling the number of subsets after every element.

optimal.complexity: O(n * 2^n) time and O(n * 2^n) space including the returned output.
optimal.description: Use bitmask enumeration. Each mask directly represents one subset, making the construction deterministic and avoiding recursive call overhead while retaining the optimal output-sensitive asymptotic complexity.

bruteForce.complexity: O(n * 2^n) time and O(n) auxiliary recursion/path space, excluding the returned output.
bruteForce.description: Use recursive backtracking. At each index, choose to exclude or include the current value. Record the current subset when all positions have been decided.

solution.spaceComplexity: O(n * 2^n) for the returned collection, with O(n) temporary space used to construct each subset.

followUps: How would you generate the same power set with backtracking?
What changes when nums can contain duplicate values?
How could you generate subsets lazily without storing the entire answer?

hidden.label: Three values spanning negative zero positive
Six distinct positive values near upper boundary
Boundary-spanning values within the allowed range

learningObjectives: Understand power-set size and exponential output.
Use bitmasking to encode include/exclude choices.
Practice backtracking and iterative subset generation.
